strengths: Novel mechanistic approach to adversarial robustness using circuit identification and causal intervention rather than black-box methods
Training-free defense method enabling seamless scalability to billion-parameter models without finetuning
Thorough empirical validation across multiple model scales (ViT-B to ViT-BigG) and diverse real-world attack benchmarks (RTA-100, Disentangling, PAINT-DS)
Consistent improvements in typographic robustness (5.5-32.78%) with minimal degradation on non-typographic benchmarks (<1%)
Convincing causal analysis through attention pattern manipulation experiment demonstrating fine-grained control over typographic vulnerability
Interesting mechanistic insights into how CLIP processes typography: sharp emergence in second half of layers, attention layers add information while MLPs compress it
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and practical contribution via released dyslexic CLIP models
weaknesses: Fundamental practical limitation: defense only protects cls token, while modern VLMs (LLaVA, IP-adapters) use spatial tokens allowing typographic information to propagate to downstream tasks, severely limiting real-world applicability

Incomplete baseline comparisons: only Defense-Prefix quantitatively evaluated in detail; other methods [18, 19, 22] lack comparison; Defense-Prefix outperforms on some metrics (Disentangling: 82.78% vs 65.00%)
Limited methodological novelty: Typographic Attention Score adapted from prior work [30], circuit construction is straightforward greedy search, relatively simple conceptually despite being effective

Evaluation concerns: no adaptive attacks tested against an adversary aware of the defense; synthetic datasets (ImageNet-100-Typo with random text placement, Unsplash-Typo with fixed bottom position) may bias head selection toward specific patterns
Arbitrary hyperparameter choices without justification: ε=0.01 threshold selected without sensitivity analysis, 5% dataset subset not motivated, unknown robustness to these choices
Incomplete ablation studies: no sensitivity analysis for threshold ε, limited exploration of circuit sparsity (4.2-10.2%), no comparison of alternative ranking criteria
Limited scope: only OpenCLIP models tested (generalization to ALIGN, LiT, SigLIP unknown); primarily zero-shot classification evaluated (retrieval, generation applications not tested)

Attention sink mechanism underexplored: mechanistically interesting finding (Appendix B) but disconnected from main narrative, mechanism explanation lacking, unclear why this pattern emerges during training
Missing deeper analysis: why CLIP learns typographic circuits unexplored, connection between circuit sparsity and vulnerability not examined, limited discussion of failure modes on certain datasets
Reproducibility concerns: relies on very recent Prisma library [29] from 2025, limited hardware specifications provided, unclear generalization beyond OpenCLIP models
